programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed
programme.desc: In a daring kidnap attempt, a small force of crack German paratroopers are poised to snatch Winston Churchill and return with him to Germany. If they succeed in their mission, it could alter the course of the war.

programme.title: Culloden
programme.desc: Camera crews capture images of war on the front lines; Peter Watkins directs.

programme.title: Britain's Lost Waterlands: Escape to Swallows and Amazons Country
programme.desc: Documentary which follows Dick Strawbridge and Alice Roberts as they explore the British landscapes that inspired children's author Arthur Ransome to write Swallows and Amazons.

programme.title: Yorkshire Wolds Way
programme.desc: The trail starts at the Humber Estuary and ends at the Yorkshire seaside resort of Filey. On the way, Paul takes in the views of the Yorkshire Wolds from the top of the Humber Bridge, learns to ride a penny farthing and searches out the spots made internationally famous by the artist David Hockney.

programme.title: Pubs, Ponds, and Power: The Story of the Village
programme.desc: Archaeologist Ben Robinson explores Lavenham in Suffolk, the best-preserved medieval village in the country. In the 16th century Lavenham was one of the wealthiest places in England, becoming rich on its woollen cloth industry, but the industry declined and the wealthy abandoned Lavenham. By the 19th century it was a place of poverty, but today it is once more a jewel of a village.

programme.title: Yellowstone: Wildest Winter to Blazing Summer
programme.desc: Patrick Aryee follows the grizzly bears that are taking a risk with the weather by leaving their winter dens early. Hungry wolves are struggling to bring down their elk prey in the unusually shallow snow. For great grey owls, it is the iciness of the snow that is hampering their hunts.

programme.title: Mike Leigh Remembers Nuts in May
programme.desc: Mike Leigh, icon of British TV and film, looks back on one of his most popular and influential television plays, 1976's classic camping comedy Nuts in May.

programme.title: Play for Today
programme.desc: Their Morris packed to the gills, the punctilious Keith and the more spontaneous Candice-Marie arrive at a Dorset campground for ten nights of idyllic bliss. It starts off pretty perfect, it's peaceful, they go sightseeing, eat vegetarian food and go in search of raw milk. Then a fellow with a loud radio pitches his tent near theirs. Things get worse when a couple arrive on a motorcycle, make noisy love in their tent and start an illegal campfire.

programme.title: The Many Faces of Alison Steadman
programme.desc: Alison Steadman talks about her impressive career, featuring archive footage and testimony from friends and colleagues. The programme progresses from her earliest appearances on screen, to what drove her choices, for good or ill, and their consequences. Contains footage and stills from programmes such as `Gavin and Stacey', `Abigail's Party', `Newshounds', `Nuts in May' and her early appearances in `Frost'.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: Why has Antarctica, the most inhospitable place on the planet, exerted such a powerful hold on the imagination of explorers, scientists, writers and photographers. From the logbooks of Captain Cook to the diaries of Scott and Shackleton, from the Rime of the Ancient Mariner to HP Lovecraft, it's a film about real and imaginary tales of adventure, romance and tragedy.

programme.title: Horizon
programme.desc: Britain's state-of-the-art Antarctic research base, Halley VI, is in trouble. It sits atop a massive slab of ice that extends far beyond the Antarctic shoreline, but the ice is breaking apart, and a huge crevasse is just 6km from the station.
